Recall the following:

- a function $f(x)$ is *even* if $f(-x)=f(x),$

- a function $f(x)$ is *odd* if $f(-x)=-f(x).$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. Therefore, we have

$$
{\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

Notice that $f(x)=\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{2}$ is an odd function. Indeed, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =\frac{{e}^{-x}-{e}^{x}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x})}{2} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{2} \\  & =-f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

So, because $f(x)=\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{2}$ is an odd function, we have

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{3}\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{2}\,\text{d}x=0.
$$
